classification.difficultyReason: Interpret an equal-length carpeting problem as the highest common factor of three corridor lengths.

content.prompt: The Guayalo Palace has three long corridors, whose lengths are $24\text{ m}$, $48\text{ m}$ and $60\text{ m}$, respectively. The decorators are designing a standard piece of carpeting that will fit an exact number of times into each corridor. What is the longest piece of carpet that they can choose?

answer.worked:
The carpet length must be a factor of all three corridor lengths.

Factors of $24$: $1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24$.

Factors of $48$: $1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,48$.

Factors of $60$: $1,2,3,4,5,6,10,12,15,20,30,60$.

The highest common factor is $12$, so the longest piece of carpet is $12\text{ m}$.
